newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close up after rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close up after rate decision.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Tuesday after the central bank said on Monday it would leave interest rates for August unchanged, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.06 pct to 110.39
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.06 pct to 110.45
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.02 pct 109.95
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.14 pct to 110.92
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 108.21
Volume including Makams was an average 162 million shekels.
"The unchanged interest rates did not affect trading today because expectations were that they would remain the same," said Ilan Doron of Solid Financial Markets.
The Bank of Israel said on Monday it was leaving unchanged at 12.7 percent its key lending rate for August. The central bank slashed its base lending rate in mid-June by 1.2 percentage points.

Doron said demand was up both for CPI-linked bonds and unlinked bonds on Tuesday. "There are different opinions in the market about what July's consumer price index (CPI) will be. Most traders believe it will be high and are going for CPI-linked bonds. But some are still buying unlinked bonds," he said.

The rise of the dollar against the shekel in June, which caused June's CPI to rise a steep 1.1 percent, has triggered fears of a series of high indices. The shekel has recovered some of its losses against the dollar in the past two weeks.
"We think July's CPI will be a relatively high 0.9 percent," Doron said. July's CPI will be published on August 15.

Doron added he expected yields to remain at current levels at least until July's CPI was published. "In the long run though we predict yields of CPI-linked long bonds to continue lower, and reach 3.7 percent by the end of the year because of the tight supply of these bonds."
Yields of CPI-linked bonds are currently ranged between 3.85 and 4.00 percent.
"The supply of CPI-linked bonds is quite dry," said Tiki Haddad of IBI Investment House. "There will be no issue of these bonds this week," she said.
New bond government issues are expected to be far lower than bond redemptions in the coming months, Doron said.
Doron added that prices of dollar-linked bonds rose on the rise of the dollar worldwide.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.53 shekels)
